title: Counting to 20: How Many Are There?
seo_title: Kindergarten Counting Worksheets: Count Objects to 20 (How Many?)
standard_text: Count to answer “how many?” questions about as many as 20 things arranged in a line, a rectangular array, or a circle, or as many as 10 things in a scattered configuration; given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten counting worksheets: count objects to 20 in a line, in rows, in a circle and spread out, use ten-frames, learn that the last number tells how many, and count out a number. 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Touch each thing once and count. The last number you say tells how many.
key_sub: 1 more is the next number. Moving things does not change how many.
body_html:
Count each thing one time

Touch each thing. Say one number for each one. The last number you say tells how many.

Things in a circle or all over

In a circle, start at one thing. Stop when you get back to it. When things are all over, mark each one as you count it.

Count 11 to 20

Fill a ten-frame first. That is 10. Then count on.

Big ideas

IdeaExample
The last number tells how many1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6: there are 6
1 more is the next number5 ducks and 1 more: 6 ducks
Moving things does not change how many6 balls in a line or in a circle: still 6

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Counting one thing two timesTouch each thing only once
Skipping a thingMark or move each thing as you count
Counting the first one in a circle againStop when you get back to the start
Counting again to say how manySay the last number: that is how many

faq.q: How high should a kindergartner count objects?
faq.a: By the end of kindergarten, children count up to 20 things in a line, in rows or in a circle, and up to 10 things that are spread out. They also count out a number, like 'give me 7 blocks'.

faq.q: My child can say the numbers but miscounts. Why?
faq.a: Saying 1 to 20 is not the same as counting things. Ask your child to touch or move each thing as they say one number. This 'one number for one thing' rule is the key skill.

faq.q: What does 'the last number tells how many' mean?
faq.a: When you count 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, the answer to 'how many?' is 5. Some children count again or say all the numbers. Ask 'So how many are there?' after they count.

faq.q: How do ten-frames help with counting to 20?
faq.a: A full ten-frame is always 10, so children do not have to count it again. They say 10 and count on: 11, 12, 13. This also gets them ready for teen numbers.
